newsitem.title: USA: IMF board urges India to be watchful on economy.
newsitem.headline: IMF board urges India to be watchful on economy.

text.p: The executive board of the International Monetary Fund, while generally pleased with India's efforts to reform its economy, said that the authorities should remain watchful, Indian IMF executive director Ramanathan Sivaraman said Wednesday.
He said the board made clear it would be a mistake for India to allow its fiscal situation to deteriorate further, since this would add to the burden of monetary policy.
Sivaraman met with reporters to talk about the IMF's annual economic review of India, which was discussed Monday at the executive board.
He said the board also made clear that India should make certain that goverment revenues kept pace with the economy and reflected actual rather than expected receipts.

In addition, the IMF seems to be raising questions about the decision of the Reserve Bank of India to announce a new credit policy, calling for a reduction in the cash reserve ratio of below 10 pct by january 1997, he said.
"They said that this should be contingent upon the price situation remaining stable and industry growing satisfactorily," he said.

Turning to overall growth, he said the board was impressed with India's progress, saying that although it has been somewhat conservative in its macro-economic management, it still has moved to higher ground and "with a little more liberalization, it should be possible for India to reach even higher levels of economic growth."
He said the government was pressing to keep the central budget deficit at or below 5.0 pct of GDP by end of fiscal 97.

The deficit in state governments is estimated to be 2.8 pct, while the deficit of public enterprises is estimated at 1.2 percent. This compared with 5.9 percent, 3.1 percent and 1.5 percent respectively in the year earlier period.
